An English crib of the Latin text, semi-literal, made for this database in 2026 with Claude, a large language model (LLM) made by Anthropic. It keeps close to the wording of the original and uses the established English of Anglo-Latin legal, liturgical and canon-law formulae. It is an aid to reading the original, not a published translation. Square brackets mark Liebermann’s additions to the text or, now and then, words supplied for the sense; “[?]” marks a doubtful reading

div.head: ECf 34.1b
div.ab: Que prius adinuente et constitute fuerunt tempore regis Eadgari, aui sui; sed post mortem eius dimisse sunt annis LX et VIII†.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 662 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.
Liebermann prints “†” after “VIII” and gives in the outer margin of the ECf retr column the dates 975–10… (the last figures are cut off in the scan used here).

note.seg: dass dem XI. Jahrh. Eadgars Recht als Ideal galt, weiss Verf. vielleicht aus Will. Malm. Reg. II 148; er missverstand vielleicht dessen Satz III 254: Cnutone defuncto, indigenæ sibi antiquum ius uendica[bant]. Er verkennt, dass Æthelred II. und Cnut Eadgars Recht wiederholten und citirten. Ebenso 34, 3

that in the 11th century Edgar’s law counted as an ideal the author knows perhaps from Will. Malm., Reg. II 148; he perhaps misunderstood that author’s sentence III 254: Cnutone defuncto, indigenæ sibi antiquum ius uendica[bant]. He fails to recognise that Æthelred II and Cnut repeated and cited Edgar’s law. Likewise 34, 3
